title: Trapping Rain Water
description: Total water trapped above a height array. Two pointers march inward; the shorter side fixes the water level on that column.

notes: The shorter side bounds the water on its column — that's why we advance it.
Update the running max BEFORE adding water; otherwise you subtract too much.
No need to precompute left/right max arrays — the two-pointer walk is sufficient.

questions.q: Why advance the pointer on the shorter side?
options: The shorter side bounds the water level for that column

questions.q: Space complexity of the two-pointer version?
Why update lMax/rMax BEFORE adding to water?
options: Otherwise lMax - height[l] could be negative
questions.explain: If you add before updating, the current bar may exceed the old max and you subtract a stale value.

exercises.prompt: Fill in the two-pointer rainwater scan.

blanks.hint: running max on the right side

L3.prompt: Write `trap(height)` returning total trapped water. Use two pointers and running max on each side. Log `trap([0, 1, 0, 2, 1, 0, 1, 3, 2, 1, 2, 1])`.
hints: Two pointers l, r. Track lMax and rMax separately.
Move whichever side is shorter — that's the side whose water level is fixed.
